scenario: Raj operates a one-person landscaping business as a sole proprietor. He has no employees and works alone. He carries no workers' compensation insurance. After Raj himself was injured, a state auditor questioned his lack of coverage and proposed the double-benefits penalty.
policy: An employer that fails to carry required workers' compensation insurance must pay a penalty equal to double the benefits owed, except where the employer is a sole proprietor with no employees other than the owner, in which case no coverage is required and no penalty applies.
question: Does the double-benefits penalty apply to Raj?
